chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Momineen (peace be upon him) ruled that the mudabbar (slave to be freed upon the master's death) is counted from the one-third (of the estate), and that it is within the man's right to revoke his bequest, so he may increase or decrease in it, as long as he has not died.

key_terms.ثُلُث: Thulutha — the 'third'; in Islamic inheritance law, a person can only bequest up to one-third of their estate
key_terms.مُدَبَّر: Mudabbar — a slave whose emancipation is conditioned on the master's death; legally treated as a form of bequest
key_terms.وَصِيَّة: Wasiyya — bequest or testament; a legal declaration of how one's property should be disposed of after death
key_terms.يَنْقُض: Yanqud — to revoke or annul; the right to revoke a bequest is a key principle here

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali rule about the mudabbar and the revocability of bequests in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling (qada') attributed to Imam Ali (AS) and reported by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). It establishes two related jurisprudential rules: first, that the emancipation of a mudabbar (a slave whose freedom is contingent upon the master's death) is taken from the bequeathable third of the estate; and second, that a person retains the right to modify their bequest — adding to or removing from it — until they die. These rulings address the legal status of conditional slave emancipation and the revocability of bequests in Islamic inheritance law.
word_analysis: the mudabbar (slave to be freed upon master's death)

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineenasws judged that the Mudabbar (slave to be emancipated (liberated) upon the death of the master), is from the third; and it is up to the man that he invalidates his bequest, so he can increase in it, and decrease from it, for as long as he had not died’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from ibn Muskan who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

’Amir al-Mu’minin issued a judgment about al- Mudabbar (slave to be set free with the death of the owner) as being part of one-third of the legacy and that a testator has the right to reduce or increase in his will as long as he is alive.’”
